projects.name: TRACE: Trajectory Inference via AI-guided Cross-view Evidence
projects.description: I develop TRACE, an LLM-guided trajectory inference agent and end-to-end Python/LangGraph package for scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
highlights: Develop TRACE, an LLM-guided trajectory inference agent that automatically identifies root states and achieves high agreement with reference trajectories across evaluated scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics datasets.

Build trace, an end-to-end Python package using LangGraph to coordinate LLM reasoning with R analysis. Integrate Seurat preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and marker analysis with Signac gene-activity estimation.
Design structured prompts and targeted molecular-evidence queries to reconcile UMAP and t-SNE views for cell-type annotation, lineage reconstruction, and root-state selection.

Develop spatial pseudotime inference using molecular evidence and spatial neighborhood graphs to distinguish repeated local processes. Estimate pseudotime from local root cells while retaining ambiguous assignments and partially resolved trajectories.
Design pPOS to jointly evaluate lineage membership and within-lineage ordering, using blockwise pair counting and inclusion-exclusion to avoid double-counting cell pairs shared across branches.

Benchmark TRACE against Monocle 3, Slingshot, and TSCAN. Investigate discrepancies in dyneval-based F1branches evaluation and reimplement the published definition over the full cell set, with diagnostics for cell coverage and branch recovery.
projects.publication_title: Visual LLM-guided trajectory inference with TRACE

projects.name: Med2State
projects.description: I develop Med2State, a Python/PyTorch deep learning model for structured patient-state representations from incomplete multimodal records and longitudinal clinical history.
highlights: Develop Med2State, a Python/PyTorch deep learning model for structured patient-state representations from incomplete multimodal records, with separate disease, procedure, and treatment channels.
Build modular encoders for demographics, measurements, structured EHR events, text, and images. Explore semantic cross-attention and low-rank fusion to integrate available evidence.
Explore temporal models for irregular visits and develop learning objectives and clinical concept readouts for longitudinal patient-state representations.

projects.name: L-STAR: Visual LLM-Guided Spatial Domain Detection
projects.description: I developed L-STAR and its Python package lstar for visual LLM-guided method selection, consensus spatial domain detection, and marker-guided domain annotation.
highlights: Developed L-STAR, a visual LLM-guided spatial domain detection framework that achieved the highest average normalized ARI across six spatial transcriptomics datasets, outperforming individual methods and fixed-method consensus.
Built lstar, a Python package integrating spatial map visualization, LLM-guided method selection, consensus clustering, and biological domain annotation with Scanpy-based marker analysis.

Designed structured prompts for repeated pairwise comparison of domain maps using tissue context and optional histology. Implemented win-rate ranking and consensus clustering in R using co-assignment matrices.

Processed study datasets with Seurat and SpatialExperiment and developed marker-guided domain annotation, distinguishing tissue regions from cell types by sampling level and retaining Unknown for insufficient evidence. Evaluated annotation agreement using BioLORD-2023 embeddings and within-dataset permutation tests.
Assessed sensitivity to ensemble size, LLM choice, color palettes, and presentation order, and quantified redundancy among selected methods.

projects.name: PaperEval
projects.description: I built OpenReview data pipelines, fine-tuned acceptance-prediction and response-grading models, and used the fine-tuned grader to evaluate generated author responses.
highlights: Built resumable OpenReview pipelines with Selenium, asynchronous requests, and structured JSON storage for papers, reviews, scores, and responses. Enriched submission metadata by extracting author contact information from PDFs with PyMuPDF.
Fine-tuned GPT-4o for paper acceptance prediction and evaluated performance with progressively richer inputs, from paper metadata to reviewer scores and review text.
Developed LLM-based agents to assess figures and tables in the context of full manuscripts and suggest improvements to clarity, readability, and presentation.
Fine-tuned GPT-4o mini as a grader for author responses, constructing proxy scoring targets from acceptance levels with bounded Gaussian noise.
Trained a reply-generation model and evaluated its responses against author replies from accepted and rejected submissions using the fine-tuned grader.

projects.name: MUDAC (Midwest Undergraduate Data Analysis Competition) 2025
projects.description: I engineered mentoring-match features and modeled match duration and closure with survival analysis, a causal Bayesian network, and a mixture-of-experts model.
highlights: Engineered features from sparse, high-dimensional numerical and text data for mentoring-match prediction, including embeddings, sentiment scores, and pairwise similarities.
Modeled match duration and closure using Cox proportional hazards regression and a causal Bayesian network.
Designed a mixture-of-experts model with regression, MLP, and Transformer experts for different feature types and a learned gating network. Compared it with random forest and XGBoost baselines.
Placed 7th in Innovation & Creativity among approximately 200 undergraduate teams at MUDAC 2025.
projects.status: 7th in Innovation & Creativity among approximately 200 undergraduate teams

projects.name: UMN & Hennepin County Public Health Equity Data Challenge
projects.description: I investigated inequities in mental-health resource access and developed a prediction interface using Hennepin County questionnaire data.
highlights: Analyzed inequities in access to mental-health resources using Hennepin County questionnaire data, applying multiple regression, ridge regression, decision trees, and causal inference methods.
Developed a tkinter interface for mental-health prediction using AdaBoost in scikit-learn.
Co-authored the analysis report and poster and placed in the top 25% of the undergraduate division.

projects.name: Overlapping Group LASSO Regression R Package Implementation
projects.description: I compared overlapping group LASSO implementations through a simulation study and implemented the optimized algorithm in C for R integration.
highlights: Compared overlapping_LeastR from the MATLAB SLEP library with oglasso in the R package VennLasso under matched problem sizes and convergence tolerances.
Designed a simulation study of 1,000 large sparse-matrix datasets with overlapping groups and used t-tests to compare implementation runtimes.
Implemented the optimized overlapping-group LASSO algorithm in C for integration with R.

work.name: Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Duke University
highlights: Help build BIOSTAT 830 resources from the ground up and quickly adapt lecture materials for its first offering in Fall 2026, bridging undergraduate statistical theory and Ph.D.-level inference.

Hold weekly office hours and grade assignments for a class of 22 students in statistical inference, asymptotic theory, and decision theory. Discuss common errors with the instructor to guide future lectures.
Prepare and verify proof-based LaTeX solutions, format and proofread slides, and manage materials in Canvas. Standardize notation and convert formulas into editable PowerPoint equations.
